requirements.requirement: WireGuard tunnel established between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense), the two routers facing each other across the transit network
requirements.summary: wg show on node2 (cmd-5e2ba22f98cf44dc) shows a live handshake to node1's public key with allowed-ips covering 10.10.10.0/24; wg show on node1 (cmd-bfd1cacfd59a42fc) shows the reciprocal handshake with allowed-ips covering 10.20.20.0/24. Both interfaces are addressed in the 10.255.255.0/30 tunnel subnet and reachable (cmd-8b120adf2b024bb9).

requirements.requirement: node3 and node4 (hosts on the two private networks) reach each other by their private addresses
requirements.summary: node3 (10.10.10.2) successfully pings node4 (10.20.20.2) with 0% loss (cmd-6e1b9a88314f4f06), and node4 successfully pings node3 (10.10.10.2) with 0% loss (cmd-b09089dac0e14bba). WireGuard transfer counters on node1 increased concurrently (cmd-44ad5e59fc8746dd), corroborating that this traffic used the tunnel.

requirements.requirement: Traffic between the routers travels inside the WireGuard tunnel (not plaintext) across the transit network
requirements.summary: tcpdump on node1's transit interface eth1, captured concurrently with a node3->node4 ping (cmd-6ee322ee4e864934), shows only UDP/51820 WireGuard packets and no plaintext ICMP (cmd-27eb1260d5434f7a). An earlier tcpdump on OPNsense's wg0 and vtnet2 (cmd-0819d62036354d92) independently confirms decrypted ICMP only appears on the tunnel interface and the private LAN, not in plaintext on the transit segment.

overall_summary: The executor established a working WireGuard site-to-site tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense), verified bidirectional private-address connectivity between node3 and node4, and confirmed via tcpdump that only encrypted UDP/51820 traffic crosses the transit link. All three material task outcomes are directly evidenced and satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol was also executed and evidenced completely and coherently for all four managed nodes, with pre-restart baselines, changed boot identities, and full post-restart recovery of addressing, routing, and WireGuard handshakes, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Hygiene is good overall; some bounded, fully-reverted discovery mutations and minor low-risk residue (an installed diagnostic package, a config backup file) were noted but do not affect functional correctness.
limitations: Firewall rule design on both routers (VyOS 'accept all forwarded traffic' rule and OPNsense 'pass all from wg0') is permissive beyond minimal necessity, though this does not violate any stated task requirement.

The fixed lifecycle 'before_prepare' snapshot for node2 shows a boot time from mid-June, inconsistent with the executor's own baseline capture of 14:27:07 on the task day; this discrepancy appears to be pre-existing infrastructure/environment behavior unrelated to executor actions and was not investigated further since it does not affect the restart-transition evidence, which is internally consistent.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to legitimate purposes: topology discovery, prerequisite addressing, WireGuard/firewall configuration, or bounded restart verification. Several transient IP-address mutations used during physical-link discovery on node1 (cmd-3132b85902784ca6, cmd-aa3cf815ab87417f), node2 (cmd-c90bd45994c94e10), node3 (cmd-65d9a1770eb042e1, cmd-f6ad8e73e05a4b07), and node4 (cmd-8335211241654032, cmd-ba3cf6f9b96b40a1, cmd-975ae78083e64f43) were fully reverted before final static configuration was applied (cmd-6e0d63ba99f34672 on node1, cmd-0a258cd61eab4061 on node2, cmd-cf35f39e9a3c4cc2 on node3, cmd-f5856b3d063c44c2 on node4) - low-risk and bounded, but counted here since they were exploratory mutations rather than read-only diagnostics. The OPNsense firewall-interface binding for the WireGuard rule went through several iterations (interface value 'wireguard' to 'wg0' to 'wireguard' to finally a dedicated opt3 assignment; cmd-2ddf2df7d36e4e03 through cmd-145d2c7563cd4cea) before converging on a working rule; each edit was superseded by the next and the final config.xml state is coherent, so this is iterative convergence rather than retained conflicting state. Minor residue: arping was installed via apt-get on node4 and left in place (cmd-887e02aa94024c4b), and a config.xml backup file was created on node2 (cmd-c62e126a8a234cbc) - both low-risk and non-destructive. No failed/conflicting services, no destructive actions, and no weakened security posture were observed in the final state.
